title: Will it fit? Four measurements to take before an air fryer arrives
desc: One listing says 13.4 inches deep, another says 16.9 inches and 26.5 pounds. Take these four measurements first — the returns desk is not a plan.
image_caption: Commissioned editorial illustration: a taped paper footprint on a counter, a tape measure, and a blank note. Not a product photograph.
body:
Every number in this guide is a number the manufacturer put on its own Amazon listing, and every one of them is bigger than most people expect. Nobody here has squeezed an appliance into a cupboard — that is the point: the listing is the only measurement source you can cite, so measure your kitchen against it.

The four measurements, and what each one kills

#MeasureHowWhat it rules out
1Counter depth, wall to front edgeTape it where the appliance will live, not where it will be photographed. Note the backsplash if there is one.A unit whose listed depth exceeds that number, no matter how good the reviews are.
2Height under the cabinet aboveMeasure to the underside of the cabinet, plus whatever clearance you will demand for steam and for the door.The tall oven-style unit if your counter is under a cabinet, and any unit whose door swings up into it.
3Width of the slot, with the door openChalk a pencil line at both edges, then open the basket or doors and measure again.A fit that only works with the drawer closed — which is not a fit.
4Where it will be stored, and its weightLift something of the same weight, at the height of the shelf you intend to use.“I'll just put it away after” plans, on the units that make that a two-person job.

What the three listings in this shop state

ProductDimensions on the listingWeight on the listingCavity, as listed
Chefman 6 Qt Dual Basket13.38"D × 11.81"W × 10.63"H13.3 lb6 Quart, described as two independent 3-Qt baskets
Chefman 8 Qt TurboFry12.75"D × 13.5"W × 10"H12.8 lb8 Quarts, one basket
Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door16.9"D × 15.8"W × 14.8"H26.5 lb26QT, stated on the same page as 24.6 litres

All nine cells were re-read from the live listings on 2026-11-20; the register row for each product links its source and read date, and the verification page keeps the two listings' internal disagreements visible (a capacity stated in quarts on one page and litres on the same page is not this site's arithmetic to settle).

The two details a spec table never tells you

  • What opens, and in which direction. Two of these are drawers that pull straight out; the French-door listing names twin doors. Front clearance is measured with the door open, or you have bought a machine you cannot load.
  • Whether the dimensions belong to your variant. One listing offers a size selector, so the depth on the page may describe a different capacity than the one you order. Re-read the dimensions on the exact variant your link lands on before you trust this table — the shop's own flagged list records why that caveat exists.
What this page deliberately does not say: no ventilation clearance figure, no “leave 2 inches” rule, no cabinet-material warning. None of the three listings states one in the fields captured, and an invented number is worse than a blank — go to the manufacturer's manual for the clearance your unit requires. This is the same rule that keeps prices and ratings blank throughout this site.

A cheap way to test the fit before you order

Cut a piece of cardboard to the listing's footprint and set it where the appliance would live. Open a door on the drawn hinge side. Stand under the cabinet with a ruler. It takes five minutes, costs nothing, and it is the same measurement a return label costs you twice.

Then check the food, not the quarts

Fit is the first filter; the second is whether your usual pan or bird actually goes inside. That is a different checklist — quarts are not servings, and two 3-quart baskets are not a 6-quart basket — so it has its own page: the capacity checklist and cleanup and counter-space trade-offs.

CARDS
faq: Is a 26QT oven-style unit too big for a normal counter?

The only number that answers that is on your wall: the listing gives 16.9 inches deep, 15.8 inches wide and 14.8 inches high, and the same page states the cavity as 24.6 litres. Measure the spot and compare — this site has not put it in a kitchen.
How much clearance do I need for ventilation?

Not on any of these listings, in the fields captured. Get it from the manufacturer's manual for the exact model, and treat any generic number you find online — including one printed here — as a guess.
Can I store an air fryer in a cupboard between uses?
That is a weight question more than a shape question: the listed weights are 13.3 lb, 12.8 lb and 26.5 lb. Lift something that heavy to the shelf height you plan to use and decide.
Why does one listing say quarts and litres on the same page?

Because the two units appear in different parts of the same listing, and this site records both instead of choosing one for you. The disagreement is on the Flagged for Review page with the action that would settle it.
Does the footprint change if I pick a different size?
It can. One listing shows a size selector, so dimensions on the page may describe another variant. Re-read the dimensions on the variant you are actually ordering.
